clinician.final_diagnosis: An elevated β-HCG level (> 1,000,000 mUI/m) along with the identification of clinical (vaginal lesion) and radiological evidence of distant metastases (bilateral pulmonary nodes) directed us toward pulmonary metastatic CC diagnosis.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old G2P1 female presented with sudden onset dyspnea and left hemithorax pain the day after normal vaginal delivery, with signs of severe respiratory distress and a suburethral vaginal lesion. Initial workup revealed a significantly elevated serum beta-HCG level of 1,254,800 mUI/m. Chest imaging (X-ray and HRCT) confirmed left-side hemothorax and bilateral pulmonary nodes (up to 41 mm in the right upper lobe and 34 mm in the left lung), suggestive of metastases. These findings, including the high beta-HCG, vaginal lesion, and pulmonary metastases, supported the diagnosis of pulmonary metastatic choriocarcinoma.
